data.name: v5.8.0
data.body:
## What's Changed

> ℹ️ **Scheduled jobs are now supported.** A job is a one-shot unit of work declared in the top-level `jobs:` element of your Compose file, run on demand or on a schedule. 
Scheduling needs **Docker Engine 29.10 or later with the jobs extension enabled** (it is off by default: `dockerd --extension-enable org.mobyproject.jobs.v0`). Manual jobs keep working on any engine, and projects that declare no jobs are unaffected.

```yaml
services:
  db:
    image: postgres
jobs:
  backup:
    image: backup-tool
    depends_on: [db]
    triggers:
      schedule:
        - cron: "0 3 * * *"
```

> * `docker compose up` (or `create`) registers the scheduled jobs with the engine, which fires them on its own clock; `docker compose down` removes them. On an engine without jobs support, `up` refuses a project with scheduled jobs before creating anything.
> * `docker compose run backup` triggers a job right away: its dependencies start first, its logs are streamed and its exit code is returned. On an engine without jobs support, it runs as a one-off service with a warning, as before.

### ✨ Improvements

**Jobs**
* Jobs: add support for one-shot and scheduled `jobs` by @glours in https://github.com/docker/compose/pull/14155

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/docker/compose/compare/v5.7.2...v5.8.0
Stamp 19.0.

data.name: RabbitMQ 4.4.1
data.body:
RabbitMQ `4.4.1` is a maintenance release in the `4.4.x` [release series](https://www.rabbitmq.com/release-information).

It is **strongly recommended** that you read [4.4.0 release notes](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/releases/tag/v4.4.0)
in detail if upgrading from a version prior to `4.4.0`.

### Minimum Supported Erlang Version

The minimum supported Erlang version for this release series is `27.0`.

[RabbitMQ and Erlang/OTP Compatibility Matrix](https://www.rabbitmq.com/docs/which-erlang) has more details on Erlang version requirements for RabbitMQ.

Nodes **will fail to start** on older Erlang releases.


## Changes Worth Mentioning

Release notes can be found on GitHub at [rabbitmq-server/release-notes](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/tree/v4.4.x/release-notes).

### Core Server

#### Bug Fixes

 * Definition import on boot could hang on Erlang 28 because of a missing dependency
   between boot steps.

   GitHub issues: [#17914](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/issues/17914), [#17915](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/17915)

 * Virtual host records written by older versions could have their limits set to `undefined`,
   which made definition export fail.

   GitHub issue: [#18137](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/18137)

 * Definition export no longer includes bindings to exclusive queues, and definition import
   skips bindings to `amq.*` queues with a warning instead of failing.

   GitHub issue: [#17838](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/17838)

 * Definition export no longer includes bindings of queues that were concurrently deleted,
   and definition import skips bindings of missing server-named queues.

   GitHub issue: [#17841](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/17841)

 * A quorum queue leader health check could report a queue with a leader as unhealthy, for example
   after a leadership change or when the node running the check did not host a replica.

   GitHub issue: [#18274](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/18274)

 * When a new quorum queue member is started, the lowest `ra` machine version among the
   reachable members is now used.

   GitHub issues: [#18053](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/issues/18053), [#18055](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/18055)

 * The quorum queue message expiration timer is now capped at one year.

   GitHub issue: [#17815](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/17815)

 * The metadata store now waits for Raft members with a capped timeout, which avoids an endless
   retry loop in some operational scenarios.

   GitHub issues: [#18114](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/issues/18114), [#18233](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/18233)

 * Classic queue CRC32 checksums are now calculated in a way that is compatible with future Erlang releases.

   GitHub issues: [#18161](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/issues/18161), [#18216](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/18216)

 * Classic queues: a crash report for a deleted queue now shows the original error.

   GitHub issue: [#18208](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/18208)

 * Message conversion between AMQP 0-9-1 and AMQP 1.0 no longer fails on `decimal`
   and `null` header values, nor on `float`, `double` and `null` annotation values
   set by the AMQP 1.0 `modified` outcome.

   GitHub issues: [#18042](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/18042), [#18156](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/18156)

 * Hourly log file rotation (for example, `log.file.rotation.date = $H30`) never rotated the file.

   GitHub issues: [#7562](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/issues/7562), [#18263](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/18263)

 * Streams now handle non-string `x-stream-filter-value` values gracefully.

   GitHub issue: [#18147](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/18147)

 * AMQP 0-9-1 header and argument tables are validated more strictly.

   GitHub issues: [#18213](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/18213), [#18243](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/18243)

 * AMQP 1.0 frames are validated more strictly.

   GitHub issues: [#17954](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/17954), [#18029](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/18029)

 * AMQP 1.0 SQL filter expressions are evaluated more defensively.

   GitHub issue: [#18302](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/18302)

 * An AMQP 1.0 session no longer crashes when its writer process has already exited
   during connection closure.

   GitHub issue: [#18070](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/18070)

 * Credential expiry handling improvements.

   GitHub issues: [#17857](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/17857), [#17979](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/17979), [#17980](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/17980)

 * [Proxy Protocol](https://www.rabbitmq.com/docs/networking#proxy-protocol) handling improvements.

   GitHub issue: [#17995](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/17995)

 * Dead lettering validates its targets more strictly.

   GitHub issue: [#18195](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/18195)

 * Channels now send `channel.close-ok` with a short socket write timeout.

   GitHub issue: [#18242](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/18242)

#### Enhancements

 * AMQP 0-9-1 channels now use flow control when sending to the connection's socket writer process.

   GitHub issue: [#18049](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/18049)

 * Closing a non-AMQP 0-9-1 connection (for example, an MQTT, STOMP, stream or AMQP 1.0 connection)
   is now cheaper on nodes with many tracked channels.

   GitHub issue: [#18139](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/18139)

 * Policy names and definitions, as well as global runtime parameter names and values, are now
   subject to size limits. The defaults are well above realistically used values.

   ```ini
   # the defaults are 1 KiB for the name and 64 KiB for the definition
   policies.max_name_length = 1024
   policies.max_definition_size = 65536

   # the defaults are 1 KiB for the name and 128 KiB for the value
   runtime_parameters.global.max_name_length = 1024
   runtime_parameters.global.max_value_size = 131072
   ```

   GitHub issues: [#18221](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/18221), [#18261](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/18261)

 * Stream segment files now enforce a minimum size of 4,096 bytes. Note that virtually all installations
   use and should use values in megabytes, not kilobytes.

   GitHub issue: [#18023](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/18023)


### CLI Tools

#### Bug Fixes

 * `rabbitmqctl reset`, `rabbitmqctl join_cluster` and similar commands are now aware of the node boot state.

   GitHub issues: [#18017](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/issues/18017), [#18081](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/18081)

 * CLI tools and peer discovery now refuse to remove cluster members that are still booting.

   GitHub issue: [#18232](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/18232)

 * `rabbitmqctl export_definitions` file permission handling improvements.

   GitHub issue: [#18083](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/18083)


### Stream Plugin

#### Bug Fixes

 * Stream protocol authentication is validated more strictly.

   GitHub issue: [#17936](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/17936)


### Management Plugin

#### Bug Fixes

 * HTTP API endpoints that accept JSON request bodies now require the `content-type` header to be `application/json`.

   GitHub issue: [#18196](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/18196)

 * Several HTTP API endpoints that previously required previleged tagging of the use now require the `administrator` tag.

   GitHub issues: [#18206](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/18206), [#18301](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/18301), [#18065](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/18065)

 * Publishing via the HTTP API is now refused when a [resource alarm](https://www.rabbitmq.com/docs/alarms) is in effect.

   GitHub issue: [#18057](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/18057)

 * Queue, stream and exchange names that are not valid UTF-8 are now rejected with a `400 Bad Request`.

   GitHub issues: [#18215](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/18215), [#18234](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/18234)

 * CORS handling improvements.

   GitHub issue: [#18032](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/18032)

 * An example `rabbitmq.conf` file could not be generated from the management plugin's schema.

   GitHub issues: [#17941](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/issues/17941), [#18256](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/18256)

#### Enhancements

 * The polling consumer (`POST /api/queues/{vhost}/{name}/get`) endpoint now limits how many messages
   and payload bytes a single request can return:

   ```ini
   # the defaults are 1000 messages and 64 MiB
   management.polling_consumer.max_messages = 1000
   management.polling_consumer.max_payload_bytes = 67108864
   ```

   GitHub issue: [#17953](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/17953)

 * HTTP API JSON request body decoding now uses less memory with larger payloads.

   GitHub issue: [#18152](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/18152)


### Prometheus Plugin

#### Bug Fixes

 * Exchange metric labels are now properly escaped.

   GitHub issue: [#17855](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/17855)

 * Several metrics that were reported as `untyped` are now reported as `gauge`.

   GitHub issue: [#17829](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/17829)


### OAuth 2 AuthN and AuthZ Backend Plugin

#### Bug Fixes

 * Scope variable substitution is now more careful with claim values.

   GitHub issue: [#17935](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/17935)

 * More robust JWT decoding error handling.

   GitHub issue: [#17966](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/17966)


### Shovel Plugin

#### Bug Fixes

 * Non-administrator users now must provide a password (or a token) in [direct URIs](https://www.rabbitmq.com/docs/uri-spec),
   including the URIs that use their own username.

   Administrators can still use direct URIs without a password.

   GitHub issue: [#18004](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/18004)

 * A shovel now drops messages that the destination refuses because they exceed its maximum message size,
   instead of restarting over and over.

   GitHub issue: [#18279](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/18279)

 * Deleting a shovel whose peer does not respond now takes at most about 10 seconds per side.

   GitHub issue: [#18086](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/18086)

 * AMQP 1.0 shovels no longer leave connections behind when connection setup times out.

   GitHub issue: [#18095](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/18095)

#### Enhancements

 * `reconnect-delay` is now validated more strictly.

   GitHub issue: [#18110](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/18110)

 * Connection timeout is now limited to 180 seconds.

   GitHub issue: [#18037](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/18037)


### Federation Plugins

#### Bug Fixes

 * In the `no-ack` acknowledgement mode, an exchange federation link acknowledged the messages
   it dropped, which led to link restarts in some scenarios.

   GitHub issue: [#18112](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/18112)

 * Updating a `federation-upstream-set` parameter restarted federation links in all virtual hosts.

   GitHub issues: [#17858](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/17858), [#18111](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/18111)

#### Enhancements

 * `reconnect-delay` is now validated more strictly.

   GitHub issue: [#18110](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/18110)

 * Connection timeout is now limited to 180 seconds.

   GitHub issue: [#18037](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/18037)


### MQTT Plugin

#### Bug Fixes

 * Retained messages were lost when the metadata store was migrated to Khepri.

   GitHub issues: [#18185](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/issues/18185), [#18186](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/18186)

 * A retained Will message with a Will Delay Interval could not be delivered to subscribers.

   GitHub issue: [#18225](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/18225)

#### Enhancements

 * The number of topic filters and user properties per packet is now limited:

   ```ini
   # the defaults are 512
   mqtt.max_topic_filters_per_packet = 512
   mqtt.max_user_properties_per_packet = 512
   ```

   GitHub issue: [#18025](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/18025)

 * Message expiration is now limited to 10 years, consistent with other protocols.

   GitHub issue: [#18141](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/18141)


### STOMP Plugin

#### Bug Fixes

 * Consumer deliveries were not included in global message rates (a regression in `4.4.0`).

   GitHub issues: [#18155](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/issues/18155), [#18168](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/18168)

 * STOMP connections were not fully integrated with connection tracking (a regression in `4.4.0`).

   GitHub issue: [#17926](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/17926)

 * The connection process heap size limit used during authentication was not lifted after
   login (a regression in `4.4.0`).

   GitHub issue: [#18122](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/18122)

 * Queue access checks for `SUBSCRIBE` frames are now consistent with other protocols.

   GitHub issue: [#17933](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/17933)

 * `CONNECT` frames that have no `login` or `passcode` header are now refused early.

   GitHub issue: [#17934](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/17934)

 * Message priority handling improvements.

   GitHub issues: [#18056](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/18056), [#18080](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/18080)

 * Transaction handling improvements.

   GitHub issue: [#18038](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/18038)

#### Enhancements

 * Message expiration is now limited to 10 years, consistent with other protocols.

   GitHub issue: [#18141](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/18141)


### LDAP AuthN and AuthZ Backend Plugin

#### Bug Fixes

 * A pooled LDAP connection is now purged after a timeout or a late reply.

   GitHub issue: [#17984](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/17984)

 * Query pre-processing and password validation improvements.

   GitHub issues: [#17934](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/17934), [#17943](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/17943), [#18018](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/18018)

#### Enhancements

 * `auth_ldap.dn_lookup_bind.password` and `auth_ldap.other_bind.password` now support
   [encrypted values](https://www.rabbitmq.com/docs/configure#configuration-encryption).

   GitHub issue: [#17879](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/17879)


### Event Exchange Plugin

#### Enhancements

 * Runtime parameter values are no longer included in the events by default.
   A new setting controls this behavior:

   ```ini
   event_exchange.runtime_parameters.include_value = false
   ```

   GitHub issue: [#18148](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/18148)


### Sharding Plugin

#### Enhancements

 * The number of shards per node is now limited to 4096.

   GitHub issue: [#17927](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/17927)


### Web STOMP Examples Plugin

#### Enhancements

 * The examples now use `@stomp/stompjs` `7.5.0`.

   GitHub issue: [#18265](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/18265)


### Erlang AMQP 0-9-1 Client

#### Bug Fixes

 * Direct channel `flush` calls now get a reply.

   GitHub issue: [#18306](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/18306)

 * The negotiated `frame_max` value is validated more strictly.

   GitHub issue: [#18108](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/18108)

 * TLS certificate and key file paths must now point to regular files.

   GitHub issue: [#18109](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/18109)


### Erlang AMQP 1.0 Client

#### Bug Fixes

 * Two processes were left running after a failed connection.

   GitHub issue: [#18093](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/18093)

 * The maximum frame size is now limited to a range between 512 bytes and 16 MiB.

   GitHub issue: [#18096](https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/pull/18096)


### Dependency Changes

 * `cowboy` was upgraded to [`2.21.0`](https://github.com/ninenines/cowboy/releases)
 * `cowlib` was upgraded to [`2.22.0`](https://github.com/ninenines/cowlib/releases)
 * `cuttlefish` was upgraded to [`3.10.0`](https://github.com/Kyorai/cuttlefish/releases)
 * `gun` was upgraded to [`2.8.0`](https://github.com/ninenines/gun/releases)
 * `jose` was upgraded to [`1.11.13`](https://github.com/potatosalad/erlang-jose/releases)
 * `ranch` was upgraded to [`2.4.0`](https://github.com/ninenines/ranch/releases)

## [28.4.0] - 2026-11-15

### Enhancements

- *(web)* Read the wiki blob excerpt from the wiki repository (#40165) (#40178)
- *(actions)* Make Actions API work with repo admin permission (#40174) (#40180)

- *(api)* Don't panic on null milestone due_on (#40171)
- *(actions)* Evaluate job `if:` against needs finished in the same pass (#40126) (#40221)
- *(web)* Build issue popup request from parsed link (#40207) (#40225)
- Allow clearing the full name in profile settings (#40186) (#40191)
- *(packages)* Return empty Chef dependencies instead of null (#40237) (#40242)
- *(deps)* Update module github.com/andybalholm/brotli to v1.2.7 [security] (#40246) (#40249)
- Upgrade Alpine base packages in Docker images (#40252) (#40253)
- Don't roll back branches on out-of-order post-receive hooks (#40110) (#40255)
- *(repo)* Mark repository as non-empty before git push returns (#40102) (#40266)
- Add missing checks to several handlers and services (#40120) (#40268)
- *(pull)* Don't add a timeline entry for pending API reviews (#40260) (#40272)

- *(deps)* Update clippie to 4.3.1 (#40293)
- Don't log network error in console when loading issue popup (#40288) (#40294)
- *(markup)* Correct character escaping at read buffer boundaries (#40209)

- *(ui)* Consistent spacing between labels (#40261) (#40330)
- Add missing checks to more handlers and services (#40131) (#40281)

data.name: BFE v1.9.0
data.body:
## [v1.9.0] - 2026-11-12

### Added
- Add `Server.ConditionEngineMode` (`LegacyFirst` default / `ExprCompatible` / `ExprOnly`): the expr condition engine with three modes — LegacyFirst keeps the generated parser as baseline with expr fallback, ExprCompatible allows mixing legacy primitives with expr syntax, ExprOnly is pure expressions; an illegal mode or illegal condition fails fast at load time
- Add `AIConf.PriceMissAction` three-state control for a missing `(model, mode)` price entry (issues #1408/#1479): `fallback_chat` (default, the previous behaviour), `bill_zero` (bill at 0 and count `PriceMissZeroBilled`), and `reject` (refuse before forwarding with 503 + `error.code=PRICE_NOT_CONFIGURED`, no upstream call, no billing, count `PriceRejected`; a missing `ModelTable` as a whole rejects the same way). Price-miss signals come in four layers: a structured throttled `PRICE_MISS` log, the counters `PriceMissZeroBilled` / `PriceFallbackUsed` / `PriceRejected` / `PriceFallbackSubItemMiss`, the access-log fields `ai_price_miss` (763, now also written on non-2xx reject rows) and `ai_price_warn` (766), and ready-made reconciliation queries
- Add a configurable key-penalty TTL (issue #1448): the AI upstream key penalty (circuit breaker, issue #1439) duration is configurable instead of hard-coded, so a 429 punishment window can be tuned per deployment
- Add reasoning-content normalization (2026-11-03): normalize `reasoning_content` / thinking-block variants across providers so downstream clients see a stable shape; the gateway skips rewriting when the request body exceeds `Server.AccessibleBodySize` and counts `ReasoningSkip` instead of touching a truncated body
- Add `AIConf.EnsureReasoningContent` (`[]string`, default empty = disabled): the model access protocols for which the gateway fills an empty `reasoning_content` on the assistant messages that sit after the last user message. Some thinking-mode upstreams require that field to be echoed back yet have turns that produce no reasoning text, so a client mirroring the upstream response gets a 400 on the next turn, and the first request after a route switch always does (the assistant turn came from the previous backend). `openai` adds `"reasoning_content": ""`; `anthropic` prepends an empty thinking block. Only `openai` and `anthropic` are accepted — `gemini` has no such field in its `contents/parts` body, so it is rejected at load time rather than silently doing nothing; each entry must also be declared by the cluster's `ModelProtocols`. The rewrite is in place (sjson): field order and every other byte are preserved, existing non-empty values are never touched, and any parse/structure failure (including a body that is not valid JSON, or one larger than `Server.AccessibleBodySize`) passes the request through unchanged. New counters `ReasoningPatched` / `ReasoningSkip` / `ReasoningFail` / `ReasoningStill400` — the last one is the exit signal: it counts requests that were patched and still got a 400, i.e. the upstream changed the contract and the switch must be cleared
- Add `Server.AIUpstreamAcceptEncoding` (`auto`/`identity`/`off`, default `auto`): how `Accept-Encoding` is rewritten on an AI upstream request, so content negotiation stays inside the coding set the gateway can decode (`gzip`, `deflate`). `auto` keeps only the decodable codings of the client's list (q values preserved, an empty intersection is left untouched, `identity;q=0` is honoured), `identity` strips compression for diagnostics, `off` keeps the previous behaviour. The rewrite only touches the outbound header: the inbound request, the access log, `mod_ai_cache` and `mod_compress` still see the client value (issue #1468)
- Add `bfe_util.NewContentDecoder` / `CanDecodeContentEncoding` / `SupportedContentEncodings`, a streaming `Content-Encoding` decoder covering `gzip`/`x-gzip` and `deflate` (zlib header sniffed, raw DEFLATE accepted). `DecodeContentEncoding` now delegates to it, so the non-streaming parse-only copy also understands `deflate` (issue #1468)
- Add the `ResStreamCompressed` / `ResStreamDecoded` / `ResStreamDecodeSkipped` / `ResStreamRawOnly` `mod_body_process` counters: how many responses carried a `Content-Encoding`, how many got the decompress-for-parsing tap, how many could not be decoded and how many degraded mid-stream. The last two mean "this request is billed by estimation", i.e. the only signal that an upstream ignored the narrowed `Accept-Encoding` (issue #1468)

### Changed
- Downgrade the normative client-close semantics of the "non-streaming boundary" clause 3 (issue #1474, product ruling 2026-11-12): when a non-streaming 200 response body is truncated mid-transfer, the connection now closes gracefully with FIN (consistent with the general proxy path and mainstream reverse proxies such as nginx), and the gateway is no longer required to abort the connection / send RST; truncation detectability relies on the response framing (a short read on a fixed-length response or a missing terminating chunk on a chunked response is detected by a conformant HTTP stack per RFC 9112 §7.1), and for close-delimited shapes (Content-Length stripped by transport-level gzip decompression, HTTP/1.0 clients) a clean EOF is indistinguishable from a complete response — an accepted residual limitation. The previously implemented abortive-close fix (closeDirectly + RST) has been reverted; the system-test acceptance criterion SC3201-TC035 A-06 is relaxed accordingly, while the `err_code=BK_READ_RESP_BODY` and billing-attribution criteria are unchanged
- Finalize the non-2xx usage counter semantics as a dual-counter scheme (issues #1409/#1480/#1493, driven by the QA re-check SC2201-TC005): suppressed estimate residue counts `Non2xxEstimateDropped`, while a non-2xx response body that carries a real usage object is reported as an observation with `ai_usage_source=parsed` (never billed) and counted by `Non2xxRealUsageKept` — the non-streaming parse gate is opened from this release (the previous `StatusOK` gate made that branch unreachable), and the billing completion gate and estimate seeding stay 2xx-only. The issue #1480 renaming to `Non2xxUsageReported` and the `failed`-source reporting were rejected and never shipped
- An AI upstream request whose client `Accept-Encoding` contains codings the gateway cannot decode no longer receives them (`Server.AIUpstreamAcceptEncoding = auto`, the default): the upstream is offered `gzip`/`deflate` only, so a client that asked for `zstd` may now receive `gzip` instead (still inside its own `Accept-Encoding`, <1% size difference). Set `Server.AIUpstreamAcceptEncoding = off` to keep the previous negotiation (issue #1468)

### Fixed
- Fix a data race on the forwarded request body size that `-race` reports intermittently in `bfe_server` (e.g. `TestForwardExpectContinue`) and therefore reddens CI: `bfe_http.(*Request).write` stores `req.State.BodySize` on the transport's `writeLoop` goroutine after the body is written, while `clusterInvoke` reads it from the serving goroutine as soon as the response header arrives. The two have no happens-before edge — an upstream that answers before reading the body, or a client that sends its body slowly (`Expect: 100-continue` is the typical shape), lets the response land first — so the pair was undefined behaviour; the store and the load are now `atomic.StoreUint32`/`atomic.LoadUint32`. No behavioural change: when the response wins the race, `req_body_len` still reads 0, which is what the (previously undefined) plain read observed anyway. The race has been present since the initial commit and is unrelated to any recent feature work
- Stop recording a fully delivered AI streaming response as a client write error when the client hangs up right after the protocol's terminal event (issue #1473): the `cancelOnClientClose` watcher closes the upstream body, the collateral read error was labelled `CLIENT_WRITE` and counted in `ErrClientWrite`, and its `err_msg` blamed the upstream (`BodyProcessError: read tcp ...`) — so 52% of production `CLIENT_WRITE` rows were normal hangs, real faults drowned in the noise, and the metric could not be alerted on. The AI send path now attributes the copy error in three states: an upstream drop stays `BK_READ_RESP_BODY` (issue #1474), a close observed after `IsResponseCompleted()` sets no `err_code` and no `ErrClientWrite` but the new access-log field `ai_client_closed_after_complete` (816) plus the `ReqAiClientClosedAfterComplete` counter, and everything else (abort before the terminal event, failed write) keeps `CLIENT_WRITE` with a direction-correct `err_msg` (`client closed connection` / `client write failed`). Also wire the last missing `ai_stream_truncated` (815) path: a clean EOF without the protocol's terminal event now marks truncation even when `NormalizeUpstreamError` is unconfigured (the injector is then the only observer), with the event parser authoritative over the byte-level markers so `data:`-only Anthropic-compatible streams are not misreported, and a cross-read overlap window so a marker split across reads is not missed. Requires `bfe-access-pb` v0.3.18
- Stop reporting an affinity binding miss as a Redis failure in the AI upstream key session affinity (issue #1472): `RedisClient.Get` reports an absent key as `redis.ErrNil`, and `redisGetBinding` passed it on as a real error, so the first request of every session (and every request after the binding TTL expires or is dropped by a 429/401) logged `aiKeyAffinity: redis get binding error[redigo: nil returned]`, counted `ReqAiKeyAffinityRedisErr` and returned early — leaving `ReqAiKeyAffinityMiss` (and `ReqAiKeyAffinityPenaltySkip`) at zero in production and the new binding unwritten until a successful forward, which also kept a session whose first request failed from ever binding. The miss is now normalized with `redis_client.IsKeyNotFound` at the read point (`redisGetBinding`, and `redisGetBatchBinding` for the batch namespace), so a plain miss takes the documented path (weighted random, write the binding, count the miss) while a real Redis failure still warns and counts
- Parse the usage of a compressed streaming (SSE) response instead of estimating it: `mod_body_process` bypassed any `Content-Encoding` body to a byte-wise pass-through, so `cache_read_tokens` stayed 0, `prompt_tokens` fell back to the request-body estimate and `completion_tokens` to the compressed-bytes estimate, and the whole prompt was billed at the input price — measured on the field at a 96% cache-hit rate that overcharges by roughly 46x and writes `ai_usage_source=estimated`. Compressed SSE now goes through `CompressedStreamDecoder`, which tees the source into a decompressor used only for parsing while the original compressed bytes are forwarded verbatim together with the `Content-Encoding` header; a decompression failure or an unsupported coding degrades to a byte-exact pass-through plus the estimate, visibly (issue #1468)
- Report a skipped `stream_options.include_usage` injection when the request body exceeds `Server.AccessibleBodySize`: the injection used to fail silently, which raised the probability of an upstream returning no usage at all (issue #1468)
- Fix a nil pointer panic that killed the request before its access log was written when a non-streaming 200 response body was truncated mid-transfer (issue #1501, PR #1504): `bfe_http.(*response).GetBodyAccessor` nil-ed `res.Body` on a failed buffered read and `mod_body_process.(*JsonDecoder).Decode` dereferenced the nil reader, so the connection-level panic was recovered without a RequestLog row and `BK_READ_RESP_BODY`/usage/quota attribution was lost entirely. The body now survives a failed accessor read (the forwarding path reports `BK_READ_RESP_BODY` / `upstreamDropped` and bills only forwarded content), and `mod_body_process` degrades safely on a nil/closed body instead of panicking. The non-stream truncation acceptance criteria (the "non-streaming boundary" clause of `2026-10-30-issue-1474`) were re-verified after deploy, which drove the client-close semantic downgrade recorded under Changed above
- Fix per-count (image/video generation) billing when the response omits the usage object (issue #1498): the generated count parsed from the response `data.#` array is adopted as recognized usage, so billing follows what the upstream actually produced (`ai_usage_source=parsed`) instead of the request-preset `n` (which overcharged when `data.# < n`) or nothing (which undercharged when `EstimateToken=false`); token-priced entries and responses carrying an explicit count are untouched
- Fix early usage becoming the billing base of a stream whose terminal event carries no usage (issue #1497): an upstream that emits usage on a non-final event and omits it on the terminating event used to be billed by the early aggregate exactly, mismatching the reported totals; early usage now only feeds the protocol context (`EarlyUsageSuppressed` marker), and billing falls back to the forwarded-content estimate per the issue #1415 yardstick
- Open the non-streaming usage parse gate for non-2xx responses so the `Non2xxRealUsageKept` counter is reachable (issues #1480/#1493, QA re-check SC2201-TC005): a real usage object on an error response is a real observation — it is now parsed, reported with `ai_usage_source=parsed` without billing, and counted; rows without a usage object keep the issue #1493 suppression (`Non2xxEstimateDropped`, token fields absent). The billing completion gate and estimate seeding stay 2xx-only, and the issue #1501 truncated-body semantics are preserved
- Make the `mod_ai_cache` JSON monitor counters (`REDIS_ERR`/`LATENCY_MS`) consistent with the Prometheus-exported values (issue #1499): a monitoring-consistency fix on the cache path; no billing behaviour change
- Deduct the full quota overage on exhaustion instead of leaving a residual (issue #1476), close EPP-scheduled long streams' billing on connection close correctly (issue #1475), and short-circuit EPP reject decisions before forwarding (issue #1482)

data.name: v1.22.4
data.body:
This is a fix release for a vulnerability (CVE-2026-97054) in Go's HTTP/1 server:

https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/iY8TY0wWgbM

> net/http: HTTP/1 server crash due to MaxBytesReader header race
>
> For HTTP/1 servers, when MaxBytesReader's limit is exceeded,
> "Connection: close" header is automatically set without synchronization,
> which might race with another header being set explicitly in the server
> handler. As a result, an HTTP/1 server that utilizes MaxBytesReader or
> MaxBytesHandler can crash due to runtime panic if its handler reads the
> request body concurrently with writing the response header.
>
> Thanks to Jakub Ciolek (https://ciolek.dev) for reporting this issue.
>
> This is CVE-2026-97054 and Go issue https://go.dev/issue/82563.

Note that our security guidance includes not running OPA with its interfaces exposed to adversarial actors, like the public internet. This is fixed regardless, if only to avoid too many spurious vulnerability checker reports.

Also note that if you build your OPA binaries yourself, this patch release does not apply to you, as you control the version of Go that's used. This patch release affects the published binaries and docker images of OPA.

data.name: v0.14.4
data.body:
### Changed

- Lowering `[auth] ACTIVATE_CODE_LIVES` or `[auth] RESET_PASSWORD_CODE_LIVES` now also shortens the lifetime of activation, email confirmation, and password reset links already sent. [#8478](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8478)

### Fixed

- _Security:_ On Windows hosts, a user creating a repository with initial files or initializing its labels could read files on the server, including the configuration file. [#8488](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8488) - [GHSA-fv2v-vwmj-j74p](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/security/advisories/GHSA-fv2v-vwmj-j74p)
- _Security:_ Referencing an issue in a commit message added a comment to it even when the pusher could not access its repository, letting anyone post into issues of private repositories. [#8486](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8486) - [GHSA-53f6-cgcf-gp6v](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/security/advisories/GHSA-53f6-cgcf-gp6v)
- _Security:_ Viewing an Org-mode file could show the contents of arbitrary files on the server, including the configuration file. [#8484](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8484) - [GHSA-hr26-3fq5-9365](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/security/advisories/GHSA-hr26-3fq5-9365)
- _Security:_ On Windows hosts, an authenticated user with write access could still write files into a repository's `.git` directory through other names for it, leading to code execution on the server. [#8483](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8483) - [GHSA-hc35-pcqw-5xjq](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/security/advisories/GHSA-hc35-pcqw-5xjq)
- _Security:_ A username containing HTML, which could come from an external login source such as LDAP, was rendered as markup on issue and pull request pages and in the dashboard issue and pull request lists. [#8482](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8482) - [GHSA-vhf5-f34f-vhq9](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/security/advisories/GHSA-vhf5-f34f-vhq9)
- _Security:_ Webhooks, repository migrations, and mirrors could reach services on the Gogs host through the IPv6 address `[::]`, bypassing the local network restriction. [#8481](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8481) - [GHSA-799r-mx22-r63q](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/security/advisories/GHSA-799r-mx22-r63q)
- _Security:_ Any signed-in user who knew the UUID of an attachment in another repository, including a private one, could move it to their own issue, comment, or release to download it, in some cases removing it from the original. [#8480](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8480) - [GHSA-p92p-7887-3g33](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/security/advisories/GHSA-p92p-7887-3g33)
- _Security:_ A password reset link could be used to sign in as the user without their password or two-factor authentication. Activation, email confirmation, and password reset links sent before upgrading no longer work. [#8472](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8472) - [GHSA-pmfh-wh5m-gmjm](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/security/advisories/GHSA-pmfh-wh5m-gmjm)
- _Security:_ Accounts with login prohibited or not activated kept repository access through access tokens, passwords, and SSH keys. [#8439](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8439) - [GHSA-f9cv-gfvg-3464](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/security/advisories/GHSA-f9cv-gfvg-3464)
- _Security:_ On Windows hosts, an authenticated user with write access could write files into a repository's `.git` directory through a crafted tree path. [#8408](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8408) - [GHSA-85m5-cfw6-3cx8](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/security/advisories/GHSA-85m5-cfw6-3cx8)
- _Security:_ Argument injection through a crafted commit or branch reference on several repository API endpoints allowed an authenticated user with read access to leak internal server details to the error logs. [#8393](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8393) - [GHSA-mxrh-2rxr-6mqc](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/security/advisories/GHSA-mxrh-2rxr-6mqc)
- _Security:_ Argument injection through a crafted branch name when creating a pull request allowed an authenticated user with write access to write files to arbitrary paths on the server. [#8390](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8390) - [GHSA-2grc-qr7q-6m36](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/security/advisories/GHSA-2grc-qr7q-6m36)
- Organization member and team actions, such as removing a member or leaving a team, failed with "Bad Request: no CSRF token present". [#8399](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/issues/8399)

<details>
<summary>Previous patch releases</summary>

## 0.14.3

### Fixed

- _Security:_ Reverse proxy authentication header was honored from any remote address, allowing user impersonation when Gogs was reachable directly. The header is now only trusted from addresses listed in `[auth] TRUSTED_PROXY_IPS`. [#8264](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8264) - [GHSA-w6j9-vw59-27wv](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/security/advisories/GHSA-w6j9-vw59-27wv)
- _Security:_ Server-side request forgery in webhook deliveries via HTTP redirects to local network addresses. [#8263](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8263) - [GHSA-c4v7-xg93-qf8g](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/security/advisories/GHSA-c4v7-xg93-qf8g)
- _Security:_ Denial of service when rendering issue references against a malformed external issue tracker URL format. [#8312](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8312) - [GHSA-4j89-2c4f-44c6](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/security/advisories/GHSA-4j89-2c4f-44c6)
- _Security:_ Stored XSS in Jupyter notebook (`.ipynb`) preview through Markdown links with `javascript:` URLs. [#8319](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8319) - [GHSA-jq8v-rmf6-65jw](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/security/advisories/GHSA-jq8v-rmf6-65jw)
- _Security:_ Missing authorization check on the attachment download endpoint allowed anyone who knew (or guessed) an attachment UUID to download files belonging to private repositories. [#8320](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8320) - [GHSA-p9f5-h3rx-j5qw](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/security/advisories/GHSA-p9f5-h3rx-j5qw)
- _Security:_ Organization team and member management actions accepted GET requests, allowing a logged-in owner to be tricked into adding an attacker to the Owners team via a crafted link. [#8321](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8321) - [GHSA-pwx3-qcgw-vh7h](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/security/advisories/GHSA-pwx3-qcgw-vh7h)
- _Security:_ SSRF via mirror address update bypassing clone address validation. [#8225](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8225) - [GHSA-wv27-2vqp-j7g5](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/security/advisories/GHSA-wv27-2vqp-j7g5)
- _Security:_ Open redirect on login and other post-action flows via the `redirect_to` query parameter. [#8322](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8322) - [GHSA-xxhq-69mf-w8cr](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/security/advisories/GHSA-xxhq-69mf-w8cr)
- _Security:_ Privilege escalation to repository owner via collaboration access mode update. [#8227](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8227) - [GHSA-4565-r4x7-hg8j](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/security/advisories/GHSA-4565-r4x7-hg8j)
- _Security:_ SSRF in repository migration and recurring mirror sync via HTTP redirects and stale host validation on stored mirror URLs. [#8324](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8324) - [GHSA-g2f5-gjr4-qjvm](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/security/advisories/GHSA-g2f5-gjr4-qjvm)
- _Security:_ Remote command execution via pull request rebase merges with crafted branch names. [#8301](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8301) - [GHSA-qf6p-p7ww-cwr9](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/security/advisories/GHSA-qf6p-p7ww-cwr9)
- _Security:_ Stored XSS in the milestone dropdown on the new issue page via crafted milestone names. [#8325](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8325) - [GHSA-vcm5-gvmp-78mp](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/security/advisories/GHSA-vcm5-gvmp-78mp)
- _Security:_ Stored XSS in Jupyter notebook (`.ipynb`) preview through `data:text/html` URIs that bypassed the sanitizer. [#8326](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8326) - [GHSA-3w28-36p9-w929](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/security/advisories/GHSA-3w28-36p9-w929)
- _Security:_ Write-level collaborators could change admin-only repository settings (issue tracker, wiki, mirror sync) via API. [#8327](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8327) - [GHSA-268j-37xf-pp52](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/security/advisories/GHSA-268j-37xf-pp52)
- _Security:_ Password reset tokens stayed valid for the account-activation lifetime, ignoring `[auth] RESET_PASSWORD_CODE_LIVES`. [#8328](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8328) - [GHSA-5c3f-6486-3g7g](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/security/advisories/GHSA-5c3f-6486-3g7g)
- _Security:_ Stored XSS in Jupyter notebook (`.ipynb`) preview through raw HTML in markdown cells. [#8330](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8330) - [GHSA-6vxv-wg6j-5qwp](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/security/advisories/GHSA-6vxv-wg6j-5qwp)
- _Security:_ Read-only Git HTTP access could be confused with write access during repository pushes. [#8331](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8331) - [GHSA-wmfg-5p4h-5fw3](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/security/advisories/GHSA-wmfg-5p4h-5fw3)
- _Security:_ Arbitrary file write outside the repository working tree via crafted upload filename routed through a committed directory symlink. [#8332](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8332) - [GHSA-89mr-xqfv-758m](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/security/advisories/GHSA-89mr-xqfv-758m)
- _Security:_ Cross-repository disclosure of Git LFS object contents by binding a known OID to another repository without proving possession of the bytes. [#8333](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8333) - [GHSA-6p9m-q3jp-47h4](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/security/advisories/GHSA-6p9m-q3jp-47h4)
- _Security:_ Remote code execution via path traversal in organization names accepted through the API. [#8334](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8334) - [GHSA-c39w-43gm-34h5](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/security/advisories/GHSA-c39w-43gm-34h5)
- _Security:_ Stalled SSH handshakes pinned a file descriptor and goroutine indefinitely. The built-in SSH server now drops connections that do not complete the handshake within 15 seconds. [#8335](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8335) - [GHSA-xp79-5mx3-jx52](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/security/advisories/GHSA-xp79-5mx3-jx52)
- _Security:_ Organization metadata and team list endpoints were reachable without authentication. [#8336](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8336) - [GHSA-744x-3838-5r56](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/security/advisories/GHSA-744x-3838-5r56)

## 0.14.2

### Fixed

- _Security:_ Denial of service in repository and wiki file listing pages via crafted file names. [#8116](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8116) - [GHSA-3qq3-668m-v9mj](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/security/advisories/GHSA-3qq3-668m-v9mj)
- _Security:_ Cross-repository LFS object overwrite via missing content hash verification. [#8166](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8166) - [GHSA-gmf8-978x-2fg2](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/security/advisories/GHSA-gmf8-978x-2fg2)
- _Security:_ Stored XSS via data URI in issue comments. [#8174](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8174) - [GHSA-xrcr-gmf5-2r8j](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/security/advisories/GHSA-xrcr-gmf5-2r8j)
- _Security:_ Release tag option injection in release deletion. [#8175](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8175) - [GHSA-v9vm-r24h-6rqm](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/security/advisories/GHSA-v9vm-r24h-6rqm)
- _Security:_ Stored XSS in branch and wiki views through author and committer names. [#8176](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8176) - [GHSA-vgvf-m4fw-938j](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/security/advisories/GHSA-vgvf-m4fw-938j)
- _Security:_ DOM-based XSS via issue meta selection on the issue page. [#8178](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8178) - [GHSA-vgjm-2cpf-4g7c](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/security/advisories/GHSA-vgjm-2cpf-4g7c)
- Unable to update files via web editor and API. [#8184](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8184)

### Removed

- Support for passing API access tokens via URL query parameters (`token`, `access_token`). Use the `Authorization` header instead. [#8177](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8177) - [GHSA-x9p5-w45c-7ffc](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/security/advisories/GHSA-x9p5-w45c-7ffc)

## 0.14.1

### Added

- Support comparing tags in addition to branches. [#6141](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/issues/6141)
- Show file name in browser tab title when viewing files. [#5896](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/5896)
- Support using TLS for Redis session provider using `[session] PROVIDER_CONFIG = ...,tls=true`. [#7860](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/7860)
- Support expanading values in `app.ini` from environment variables, e.g. `[database] PASSWORD = ${DATABASE_PASSWORD}`. [#8057](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8057)
- Support custom logout URL that users get redirected to after sign out using `[auth] CUSTOM_LOGOUT_URL`. [#8089](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8089)
- Start publishing next-generation, security-focused Docker image via `gogs/gogs:next-latest`, which will become the default image distribution (`gogs/gogs:latest`) starting 0.16.0. While not all container options support have been added in the next-generation image, the use of current legacy Docker image is deprecated, it will be published as `gogs/gogs:legacy-latest` starting 0.16.0, and be completely removed no earlier than 0.17.0. [#8061](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8061)

### Changed

- The required Go version to compile source code changed to 1.25.
- The build tag `cert` has been removed, and the `gogs cert` subcommand is now always available. [#7883](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/7883)
- Switched to pure-Go SQLite driver, CGO is no longer required to compile Gogs. [#7882](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/issues/7882)
- Updated Mermaid JS to 11.9.0. [#8009](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8009)
- Halt the repository creation and leave the directory untouched if the repository root already exists. [#8091](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8091)

### Fixed

- _Security:_ Unauthenticated file upload. [#8128](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8128) - [GHSA-fc3h-92p8-h36f](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/security/advisories/GHSA-fc3h-92p8-h36f)
- _Security:_ Protected branch bypass in web UI. [#8124](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8124) - [GHSA-2c6v-8r3v-gh6p](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/security/advisories/GHSA-2c6v-8r3v-gh6p)
- _Security:_ Authorization bypass allows cross-repository label modification. [#8123](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8123) - [GHSA-cv22-72px-f4gh](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/security/advisories/GHSA-cv22-72px-f4gh)
- _Security:_ Cross-repository comment deletion. [#8119](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/pull/8119) - [GHSA-jj5m-h57j-5gv7](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/security/advisories/GHSA-jj5m-h57j-5gv7)
- 500 error on repository watchers and stargazers pages when using MSSQL. [#5482](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/issues/5482)
- Submodules using `ssh://` protocol and a port number are not rendered correctly. [#4941](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/issues/4941)
- Missing link to user profile on the first commit in commits history page. [#7404](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/issues/7404)
- Unable to delete or display files with special characters in their names. [#7596](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/issues/7596)
- Docker healthcheck fails when `HTTP_PROXY` or `HTTPS_PROXY` environment variables are set. [#7529](https://github.com/gogs/gogs/issues/7529)

</details>

data.body:
### November 12, 2026

SECURITY:

* core/acl: Harden explicit deny rule evaluation by matching requested paths case-insensitively.

CHANGES:

* auth/alicloud: Update plugin to [v0.24.1](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault-plugin-auth-alicloud/releases/tag/v0.24.1)
* auth/cf: Update plugin to [v0.24.1](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault-plugin-auth-cf/releases/tag/v0.24.1)
* auth/jwt: Update plugin to [v0.27.2](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault-plugin-auth-jwt/releases/tag/v0.27.2)
* auth/kerberos: Update plugin to [v0.18.1](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault-plugin-auth-kerberos/releases/tag/v0.18.1)
* auth/oci: Update plugin to [v0.22.1](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault-plugin-auth-oci/releases/tag/v0.22.1)
* core: Bump Go version to 1.27.4
* core/acl: Fix an issue where explicit deny policy rules were not enforced against case variants of the denied path. Explicit deny rules now also match the requested path case-insensitively, subject to the usual rule specificity. For example, a deny on `secret/data/example` now also denies requests to `secret/data/EXAMPLE`.
* database/couchbase: Update plugin to [v0.17.1](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault-plugin-database-couchbase/releases/tag/v0.17.1)
* database/elasticsearch: Update plugin to [v0.21.1](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault-plugin-database-elasticsearch/releases/tag/v0.21.1)
* database/mongodbatlas: Update plugin to [v0.18.1](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault-plugin-database-mongodbatlas/releases/tag/v0.18.1)
* database/redis: Update plugin to [v0.9.1](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault-plugin-database-redis/releases/tag/v0.9.1)
* database/snowflake: Update plugin to [v0.17.1](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault-plugin-database-snowflake/releases/tag/v0.17.1)
* proxy/agent: Custom plugins or integrations that return interactive HTML through Agent or Proxy will no longer render interactively in a browser.
* secrets/alicloud: Update plugin to [v0.23.1](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault-plugin-secrets-alicloud/releases/tag/v0.23.1)
* secrets/azure: Update plugin to [v0.28.5+ent](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault-plugin-secrets-azure/releases/tag/v0.28.5+ent)
* secrets/keymgmt: Update plugin to [v0.20.2+ent](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault-plugin-secrets-keymgmt/releases/tag/v0.20.2+ent)
* secrets/mongodbatlas: Update plugin to [v0.18.1](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault-plugin-secrets-mongodbatlas/releases/tag/v0.18.1)
* secrets/terraform: Update plugin to [v0.15.1](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault-plugin-secrets-terraform/releases/tag/v0.15.1)

IMPROVEMENTS:

* core: Include the namespace ID in mount setup failure logs
* core: Update github.com/go-jose/go-jose/v4 to v4.1.6 and golang.org/x/net to v0.62.0
* ui: Show "Never" as the last Vault rotation on the LDAP role credentials page when a static role has not been rotated, instead of a date in year 0001.

BUG FIXES:

* Transit (enterprise): Fix cache bug that led to non-zero `auto_rotate_period` values being written to the cache with managed keys
* agent/pki-external-ca (enterprise): Fix premature certificate reissuance on auto-auth re-authentication so certificate renewal respects `percent_renew_before_expiry` instead of being triggered by token updates.
* audit: Fixed a bug where Vault returned HTTP 500 when a large response (e.g. a PKI ?help=1 request) could not be written to a syslog audit device due to the OS Unix datagram socket size limit (EMSGSIZE / ENOBUFS). The syslog sink now splits oversized audit payloads into safe-sized chunks and retries transiently full socket buffers.
* audit: Fixes a panic that can occur when audit broker not initialized during teardown.
* auth/approle: Reject expired SecretIDs during login instead of relying on periodic tidy cleanup.
* auth/spiffe (enterprise): Fix an issue where renewable tokens were not being renewed
* core (enterprise): Fix a panic and partial namespace creation when the root agent-registry mount is unavailable
* core/census (enterprise): Fix the `previous_month_complete` census gauge reporting 0 in the first month after the billing start date auto-rolls, so the previous billing cycle's final client count is reported.
* core/plugin: Fix an issue where external secrets engine and auth plugins remained read-only after failing to load during startup or unseal. Operators can now restore the missing binary or registration and reload the plugin to resume writes without restarting Vault.
* core: Fix an issue where policy path matching could be inconsistent for requests that differ only by a trailing slash.
* identity: Use the reporting conflict resolver only while reloading in case-sensitive mode, to avoid collecting duplicates after unseal.
* pki-external-ca: Fix premature deletion of revoked certificate records during tidy; revoked orders are now retained until the certificate's NotAfter date rather than the ACME order expiry
* secrets/azure: Continue permanent application cleanup when the active application is already absent, allowing later cleanup attempts to retry the purge.
* secrets/azure: Retry transient Microsoft Graph 403/404 errors when adding newly created service principals to Azure groups.
* secrets/kv: Fixed an issue in KV v1 where writing a secret path containing consecutive slashes caused list operations to return "/" as a directory entry, producing an infinite loop in the Vault UI breadcrumb.
* tpm: tpm auth now respects the InsecureSkipVerify option
* ui: Fix the database overview page to list both dynamic and static roles and allow credential generation, and restore the Roles tab for users with only static-role permissions
* ui: fixes pagination on entities list table
* vault proxy: Support tpm method in the auto_auth block to match parity with agent.

data.name: Release v2.15.3
data.body:
## Changelog

Refer to the [2.15 Upgrade Guide](https://docs.nats.io/release-notes/upgrade-to-2.15) for backwards compatibility notes with 2.14.x.

### Go Version

- 1.27.4

### Dependencies

- github.com/nats-io/jwt/v2 v2.8.3 (#8861)
- github.com/nats-io/nkeys v0.4.17 (#8861)
- github.com/antithesishq/antithesis-sdk-go v0.9.0-default-no-op (#8885)
- github.com/klauspost/compress v1.20.4 (#8885)
- golang.org/x/sys v0.50.0 (#8885)

### Added

General

- Account subject mappings, imports, exports and leafnode remote permissions now support the `{{account-hash()}}`, `{{account-hash-import()}}` and `{{account-hash-leaf-remote()}}` subject mapping functions (#8670)
- TLS configuration now supports `verify: optional`, and the command line supports `--tlsverify=optional`, verifying client certificates when provided while allowing clients without certificates (#8812, contributed by @macphersonjamie)
- Leafnode connections now support a configurable `ping_interval` (#8718, contributed by @stackedbyaradhya)
- Gateway connections now support a configurable `ping_interval` (#8717, contributed by @stackedbyaradhya)
- The command line now supports `-t --test_reload <file>` to check whether a configuration change can be reloaded or requires a restart, returning exit code 3 when a restart is required; embedded servers can use `CheckReload` and `CheckReloadOptions` (#8829)

Monitoring

- Healthz now supports `leaf-remotes-connected=true`, returning an unavailable status until every enabled solicited leafnode remote is connected (#8735, contributed by @edjeffreys)

### Improved

General

- Route, gateway and leafnode connection logs now include remote destinations (#8755)
- Account import failures now log their reasons at error level (#8771)
- Gateway connections now validate protocol operations consistently with route connections (#8780)
- Clients authorized by auth callout can no longer publish or subscribe to the auth callout request subject or the server's auth callout reply inboxes

JetStream

- Filestore subject matching and pending message calculations now avoid unnecessary scans and stop earlier when matches are found (#8784, #8803, #8806, #8808, #8813)
- Looking up the last sequence for a subject no longer requires loading the message, reducing work for stream operations and fast batch publishing (#8807)
- Filestore scans with single or multiple subject filters now avoid copying messages that do not match (#8854, #8855)
- Consumer redelivery queues no longer copy all remaining entries on each dequeue, reducing delays to delivery and acknowledgement processing with large redelivery backlogs (#8635, contributed by @as-clearview)
- Filestore scans with multiple subject filters now handle message blocks with many deleted messages more efficiently (#8864)
- Filestore subject scans and filtered pending-message counts now skip contiguous ranges of deleted messages (#8875, #8877)
- Loading filestore message blocks now avoids fully parsing messages when checking for `Nats-TTL` and `Nats-Schedule` headers (#8870, contributed by @adios-404)

### Fixed

General

- Lame duck mode is no longer skipped when `SIGTERM` follows `SIGUSR2` immediately, and servers continue to deliver their own replies after the lame duck event (#8750)
- Configuration reloads no longer disconnect clients authorized by auth callout when their permissions have not changed (#8759)
- Auth callout user JWT names and tags are now propagated to client information (#8720, contributed by @steve-weiland)
- Configuration reloads now wait for server startup to finish (#8728, contributed by @edelmanjm)
- Connz totals now correctly reflect user, MQTT client and subject filters (#8753, contributed by @NitinKumar004)
- Connz and Subsz pagination no longer repeats or skips entries, including connections with equal sort values (#8770)
- Windows PDH queries are now released if performance counter initialization fails (#8777, contributed by @cvas22)
- Auth callout requests are now rejected safely when system account eventing has already shut down (#8804, contributed by @davidfarah2003)
- Wildcard characters inside a subject token are no longer treated as wildcard tokens or allowed to cause subject matching collisions (#8765)
- Account updates no longer unnecessarily recheck importers when export revocations have not changed (#8851)
- Configuration checks with `-t` now apply command line flags and validate options consistently with server startup (#8829)
- Duplicate non-queue subscriptions received over routes no longer leak interest to leafnodes and gateways (#8846)
- Gateway accounts in interest-only mode no longer stop receiving messages when an in-flight message races with removal of the last subscription (#8853, contributed by @paulwe)
- Encrypted auth callouts are now rejected when the server has no XKey available (#8878)
- The auth callout account now defaults to `$G` when auth callout is configured through programmatic options, consistently with the configuration file
- Auth callout subject denies are no longer dropped when default permissions are updated
- User JWT payload and subscription limits are now enforced for clients authorized by auth callout and for MQTT clients
- Duplicate auth callout replies no longer block the sender's read loop
- Auth callout now enforces the `src` restriction of the returned user JWT

JetStream

- Consumer info requests no longer report success for assignments that have not been committed (#8741)
- Push consumers with a `RateLimit` no longer stall indefinitely when a message exceeds the rate limiter burst size (#8748)
- Stream scale-up from R1 can now make progress under continuous writes, and scale-down no longer stalls on peers that were never added as members (#8762)
- Stalled stream restores now report failure through the restore completion advisory, consistently with other failed restores (#8691, contributed by @akarazhev)
- JetStream no longer shuts down prematurely during server shutdown or lame duck mode (#8708, contributed by @yousefissa)
- Raft meta-group setup failures now stop the write-ahead log instead of leaking it (#8722, contributed by @clwluvw)
- Leader transfers now retry promptly when the selected successor is slow, prefer caught-up peers and avoid persisting the same term and vote twice (#8751)
- Interest retention cleanup no longer purges a stream when a consumer has a zero check floor, and compaction is bounded by the stream's last sequence (#8757, contributed by @tsite)
- Filestore `MultiLastSeqs` no longer skips matching subjects (#8769)
- Fixed a directory creation race when enabling account storage concurrently with stream creation (#8767, contributed by @ansh0014)
- Deleting a stream no longer races with account directory cleanup (#8774, contributed by @ansh0014)
- Sources no longer discard the remainder of a batch when one sourced message is rejected (#8772)
- Pull requests made through service imports are now removed when the requester loses interest, even while response wildcard interest remains (#8797)
- Consumers no longer deliver while a reset is in flight or report later deliveries in reset responses, and durable mirrors and sources no longer skip messages after a reset or stale delivery (#8802)
- Memory store purge and last-sequence scans are now bounded by the possible sequence range (#8815)
- Raft health checks now wait for the leader's initial data to be applied, remain stable between heartbeats and during leader changes, and allow newly assigned replicated streams and consumers time to start (#8817)
- Resuming a paused consumer now wakes its delivery loop immediately, allowing pending pull requests and push deliveries to proceed (#8791)
- `AckAll` acknowledgements are no longer ignored after acknowledging a redelivered message (#8839)
- Filestore recovery failures now return the original error instead of panicking, preserve existing stream data and avoid incorrect storage accounting (#8844, contributed by @rleungx)
- Streams and consumers with unsupported configuration values are now correctly marked offline, updates are rejected by meta leaders that cannot support them, and internal proposals preserve their stored configurations (#8843)
- Paused Raft followers can now request newer snapshots and compact their logs while catching up, preventing unbounded log growth and excessive memory use when replay resumes (#8842)
- Filestore recovery scans now persist per-message state indexes even if no new messages are published, and backward subject scans skip irrelevant blocks (#8849)
- Clustered health checks now report write errors on R1 streams (#8850)
- Removed peers in unmanaged Raft groups can no longer rejoin as leader (#8847)
- Scaling streams and consumers to or from R1 no longer loses writes or acknowledgements during the transition or violates atomic batch guarantees (#8766)
- Resetting consumers with the `last_per_subject` delivery policy now rebuilds the last-message-per-subject selection, preserves the correct delivery position after leader changes, and reports lookup errors instead of ignoring them (#8862)
- Filestore encryption key creation failures no longer leak file descriptors (#8873)
- The filestore access-time worker now shuts down reliably when the last store closes, preventing worker leaks or stopped timestamp updates when stores are reopened (#8794, contributed by @ajaykr0905)
- Rebuilding message deduplication state now skips deleted messages and expires restored entries at the end of their original duplicate window (#8874)
- Restoring a stream from a V2 snapshot now rebuilds message deduplication state, restoring duplicate detection and `Nats-Expected-Last-Msg-Id` checks without a server restart (#8871, contributed by @muhadyan)
- Reply subjects, deliver subjects and service import aliases can no longer be used to make the server issue JetStream requests on a user's behalf
- JetStream domain names `ACK`, `FC`, `SNAPSHOT` and `EVENT` are now rejected, since they clash with other JetStream subjects

Leafnodes

- Isolated spoke leafnodes no longer forward downstream leafnode interest to their hubs, and avoid collecting interest that cannot be forwarded (#8749)
- Leafnode interest is now withdrawn correctly when an outbound gateway connection closes (#8758)
- Fixed a data race when reading route leafnode origin support (#8779)
- Leafnode `deny_imports` no longer drops replies to hub requests, and account JWT or default permission updates no longer lose leafnode interest or reset permissions incorrectly (#8800)
- Leafnode connections no longer become stale when a hub sends many subscriptions during connection setup (#8811)
- Leafnode connections closed during acceptance are now removed from the server's connection list, preventing inflated leafnode counts and stale Leafz entries (#8838, contributed by @rnikhori)
- Enforcing account leafnode connection limits no longer risks a deadlock when processing remote connection counts (#8873)
- Inbound leafnode messages on JetStream ack subjects are no longer exempt from leafnode permission checks
- Hub leafnode connections now keep their own copy of the import and export permissions advertised to the remote, instead of sharing them with the user's permissions

Routes

- Routes without pooling now validate the route pool index correctly (#8782)

### Complete Changes
